alerts.title: J&K govt tally: 24,416 houses and 5,373 roads damaged in 2025-26/2026-27 floods, Udhampur and Rajouri worst-hit
alerts.summary: A government reply tabled this week put cumulative flood/cloudburst damage across Jammu & Kashmir at 24,416 residential structures (23,470 in Jammu division, 946 in Kashmir division), 5,373 roads (5,084 Jammu, 289 Kashmir) and 4,183 water-supply schemes, with 106,322 hectares of crop area hit. Udhampur (6,997 houses), Rajouri (4,781) and Jammu district (2,718) are worst-affected in Jammu division; Pulwama (289) and Budgam (271) lead in Kashmir. The government said temporary restoration of 2025-26 damage is complete with permanent works underway, while 2026-27 damage is still being restored.
alerts.impact: Treat Udhampur, Rajouri and Jammu-district rural pincodes as running on degraded, partially-restored roads through the winter — keep an extended SLA buffer for LM/FM there and avoid committing new capacity until permanent road restoration is confirmed complete in each block.

alerts.title: Uttarakhand red alert: Bageshwar, Nainital, Pithoragarh on Sep 26; Dehradun, Haridwar on Sep 27 as western disturbance moves in
alerts.summary: IMD has placed Bageshwar, Nainital and Pithoragarh under a red alert for 26 September, shifting to Dehradun and Haridwar on 27 September, as a western disturbance brings a fresh spell of severe weather to northwest India. Heavy downpours could continue through 28 September with a risk of flooding or landslides, alongside thunderstorms, lightning and gusty winds.
alerts.impact: Pre-emptively buffer hill-district LM in Bageshwar, Nainital and Pithoragarh for 26 September and Dehradun/Haridwar plains routes for 27 September; hold non-essential linehaul on hill roads (already fragile after the Sep 17 Pithoragarh-Tanakpur NH-9 damage) until the red-alert window passes on 28 September.

alerts.title: Himachal Pradesh braces for fresh rain spell Sep 26-29, adding to already-damaged hill roads
alerts.summary: IMD forecasts a fresh spell of rainfall across Himachal Pradesh from 26 to 29 September, even as the state's monsoon rainfall for the season remains about 13% below normal. The fresh rain risks reactivating slide-prone stretches already flagged in Mandi, Kullu and Kangra districts.
alerts.impact: Extend the existing Mandi-Kullu-Kangra ghat-road SLA buffer through 29 September; avoid pre-positioning extra LM capacity on Chailchowk-Tattapani and Manikaran-Barshaini stretches until the fresh spell passes.

alerts.title: Bengaluru bandh called for Sep 26 over Cauvery water release to Tamil Nadu; pro-Kannada outfits shut trade, transport
alerts.summary: Pro-Kannada organisations and the Kannada Okkuta have called a Bengaluru bandh for 26 September protesting the release of Cauvery water to Tamil Nadu, with trade associations and auto-taxi unions extending support. Markets in the city's core commercial pockets and several transport operators are expected to stay shut for the day, though essential services are exempt.
alerts.impact: Expect FM pickup failures across core Bengaluru trading pockets (Chickpet, KR Market, Avenue Road belt) and slower LM city-wide on 26 September; hold non-essential dispatch/pickup in the CBD until evening and confirm rider availability before committing OFD SLAs for the day.

alerts.title: Two spans of Pamuleru stream bridge near Rajupeta (Mulakalapalli mandal) washed away — Palvoncha–Mandalapalli traffic halted
alerts.summary: Floodwaters in the Pamuleru stream washed away two spans of the bridge near Rajupeta in Mulakalapalli mandal of Bhadradri Kothagudem district, completely stopping traffic between Palvoncha and Mandalapalli. Kothagudem is among five Telangana districts under a red alert until 26 Sep, so restoration is unlikely in the short term.
alerts.impact: Mark Mulakalapalli-mandal villages reachable only via Palvoncha–Mandalapalli as temporarily non-serviceable; reroute Palvoncha/Kothagudem LM via longer alternate roads with a 1-2 day SLA buffer. Hold FM pickups from sellers in the mandal until an alternate route is confirmed.

alerts.title: Kattaleru stream in spate cuts off 20 villages between Vinagadapa and Thotamoola; flash floods across NTR district
alerts.summary: The overflowing Kattaleru stream cut off road access to about 20 villages between Vinagadapa and Thotamoola in NTR district. NewsMeter reported flash floods at several locations in NTR district, with streams and canals overflowing onto major roads and a car carrying a local cooperative society president and his wife swept away. Vijayawada's low-lying areas are waterlogged and paddy between Vijayawada and Rajahmundry is submerged; more heavy rain is forecast for NTR, Krishna, Guntur, Bapatla, Palnadu and Prakasam on 25 Sep.
alerts.impact: Flag the Vinagadapa–Thotamoola cluster (Gampalagudem/Tiruvuru side of NTR district) as non-serviceable until the stream recedes; add 24-48h buffer to Vijayawada rural LM and avoid causeway routes. Watch Vijayawada hub inbound linehauls on 25 Sep.

alerts.title: Floodwater enters Anakapalli RTC complex and railway bridge; Vizag's Tulasi Nagar logs 236 mm, Gajuwaka low-lying areas inundated
alerts.summary: Andhra Pradesh recorded 100 mm+ rain at 80 locations in 24 hours, led by Visakhapatnam Rural's Tulasi Nagar (236 mm), Madhurawada (218 mm) and Seethammadhara (205 mm). Floodwater entered the Anakapalli RTC bus complex and the railway bridge area, and strong winds uprooted 74 electric poles and damaged 50 houses at Chintalapadu. Visakhapatnam MLA Palla Srinivasa Rao toured flood-hit parts of Gajuwaka on 24 Sep.
alerts.impact: Expect 24-48h delays at Visakhapatnam and Anakapalli LM hubs (Madhurawada, Gajuwaka, Anakapalli town pincodes); stagger FM pickups from Vizag industrial sellers and confirm power at sort centres. Avoid underpasses and the Anakapalli railway-bridge stretch for linehaul.

alerts.title: Godavari at Bhadrachalam forecast to reach Warning Level-I by 26 Sep afternoon and Level-II by night
alerts.summary: Andhra Pradesh officials said on 24 Sep that the Godavari at Bhadrachalam is likely to reach Warning Level-I by the afternoon of 26 Sep and Warning Level-II that night, as heavy inflows are expected into Godavari-basin reservoirs including Sabari, Indravati, Yeleru, Tandava, Yerrakalva, Pampa and Meghadrigadda. CM Naidu told officials to fill tanks and reservoirs with the available flows.
alerts.impact: Pre-position stock and plan for 2-3 days of disruption in Bhadrachalam, Burgampadu, Kunavaram, Chintoor, VR Puram and Polavaram-area pincodes (Godavari agency villages that routinely get cut off at Level-II). Pull forward deliveries due in the Bhadrachalam belt to 25 Sep where possible.

alerts.title: Koraput's Dasmantpur block: 3 ft of water over Damjodi bridge (Nandigaon GP); Haridaphut bridge under water, ~20 villages hit
alerts.summary: In Dasmantpur block of Koraput, about three feet of water was flowing over the bridge near Damjodi village under Nandigaon panchayat, stranding vehicles on both sides. Water also accumulated over the bridge near Haridaphut under Pindapadar panchayat, on the road linking Dasmantpur police-station square with Adimunda square — the lifeline for about 20 villages of Pindapadar and Duarashuni panchayats to Koraput market. Koraput remained under red warning to 25 Sep and the collector has shut all schools and anganwadis on 25 Sep.
alerts.impact: Hold LM to Pindapadar/Duarashuni/Nandigaon GP villages (Dasmantpur block) until water recedes; the Dasmantpur–Adimunda road is the only route. Add 48h SLA buffer to Koraput district and expect FM delays for Jeypore/Koraput sellers.

alerts.title: Puri declared 'red zone' with sea-bathing ban for two days; Koraput shuts all schools and anganwadis on 25 Sep
alerts.summary: Odisha Fire Services said Puri has been designated a 'red zone' for two days as the sea turned extremely rough, deploying 98 lifeguards and banning sea bathing. The Koraput collector ordered all schools up to Higher Secondary and all anganwadi centres closed on Friday, 25 Sep, amid a continuing heavy-rain forecast. Earlier, a fallen tree on the Jatni–Pipili main road near Mathasahi stranded commuters for hours before fire services cleared it. Evening update (25 Sep): the Alipore/regional met offices confirm the system has fully weakened into a depression over south interior Odisha, so the acute cyclone-watch phase is over, but the residual rain belt keeps Koraput's interior roads hazardous into the evening of 25 Sep.
alerts.impact: Mainly a watch signal: coastal Puri LM is running but expect wind/tree-fall delays on Khordha–Puri roads; schools-shut signals in Koraput point to continued hazardous interior roads on 25 Sep — keep Koraput buffers in place.

alerts.title: NHAI bars heavy vehicles on Kanpur's Jajmau Ganga bridge for repairs; Lucknow–Kanpur traffic diverted via Ganga Barrage till 13 Dec
alerts.summary: NHAI has stopped heavy-vehicle movement on the Jajmau Ganga bridge in Kanpur for repair work. UPSRTC buses from Lucknow no longer go from the Unnao bypass straight to Jajmau; they now run via Marhla chauraha, Saraiyan crossing and the Ganga Barrage to Jhakarkati, adding about 15 km (fare raised from Rs 123 to Rs 145). The diversion is to remain in force until 13 December.
alerts.impact: Lucknow–Kanpur linehauls and Unnao-side FM milk runs should plan on the Ganga Barrage route (+15 km, extra congestion) until mid-December; re-baseline Kanpur hub cut-off times and inform carriers' Unnao/Jajmau LM teams. Heavy trucks may face slow-downs around Company Bagh/GT Road.

alerts.title: Mangtabong village landslide in Yuksom hits 12 households; NH-10 at 20th Mile Bardang reopened only for one-way traffic
alerts.summary: After a day-long clearance of a mudslide that blocked NH-10 at 20th Mile, Bardang (a truck was stuck in the debris), the highway was opened for one-way traffic; the 30th Mile stretch was also temporarily opened with clearance continuing. Drivers said the alternate Singtam–Swany–Duga–West Pendam road is in poor shape. Separately, a major landslide at Mangtabong village (Tsong Dubdi ward, Yuksom Bazar) damaged houses and killed livestock, affecting 12 households; 17 people are in a relief camp at Siru Dara.
alerts.impact: Gangtok-bound linehauls from Siliguri should plan for one-way convoy delays at Bardang/30th Mile; keep 24h buffer for Gangtok, Singtam and Rangpo LM. Yuksom (West Sikkim) deliveries should be held or consolidated until local roads are cleared.

alerts.title: Orange alert for Darjeeling, Jalpaiguri, Alipurduar on 25 Sep; high tides spill into Mandarmani, fishing banned off Digha
alerts.summary: The weather office forecast heavy to very heavy rain in North Bengal and Sikkim on 24-25 Sep, with Darjeeling, Jalpaiguri and Alipurduar on orange alert for 25 Sep and a raised risk of landslides and road blockages on NH-10. On the coast, gusty winds hit Digha and Mandarmani, the sea spilled into parts of Mandarmani, and fishermen are barred from going to sea along Digha, Shankarpur, Junput and Petuaghat. Kansabati Dam in Bankura logged 100 mm in 24 hours.
alerts.impact: Watch Siliguri–Darjeeling/Kalimpong and Dooars (Jalpaiguri, Alipurduar) LM on 25 Sep for landslip or waterlogging delays ahead of the Puja volume ramp-up; keep East Midnapore coastal pincodes (Digha, Ramnagar, Contai) on a 24h buffer.

alerts.title: Vizianagaram: power supply suspended in Therlam, Badangi, Denkada as gusty winds and rain lash district
alerts.summary: Heavy rain with gusty winds from the deep depression that crossed near Kalingapatnam hit parts of Vizianagaram district on September 24, including Therlam, Badangi and Denkada mandals, where power supply was suspended as a precaution. Educational institutions in Srikakulam and several other districts were given holidays on Thursday and Friday (Sep 24-25).
alerts.impact: Expect LM delays and weak phone/scan connectivity in Therlam, Badangi and Denkada (Bobbili–Vizianagaram belt) while power is off; check DC/sortation backup power in the Vizianagaram cluster, allow OFD cut-off relaxation for Sep 24-25 and hold COD-heavy rural routes where riders cannot top up devices.

alerts.title: South coastal AP: heavy rain forecast Sep 25 for NTR, Krishna, Guntur, Bapatla, Palnadu, Prakasam; NTR flash floods
alerts.summary: As the weakening depression moves inland, heavy rainfall is likely at one or two places in NTR, Krishna, Guntur, Bapatla, Palnadu and Prakasam districts on September 25. On September 24, flash floods hit several locations in NTR district with streams and canals overflowing onto major roads, and hundreds of acres of paddy were submerged between Vijayawada and Rajahmundry.
alerts.impact: Rain risk shifts south from Srikakulam to the Vijayawada–Guntur–Ongole corridor on Sep 25: pre-position FM pickups in Vijayawada/Guntur before noon, watch canal-side low-lying roads in NTR district, and keep SLA buffer for Bapatla, Narasaraopet (Palnadu) and Ongole (Prakasam) LM routes.

alerts.title: Gangtok: odd-even vehicle curbs on NH-10 Ranipool (Mayfair Jn)–Zero Point stretch under HC-ordered review
alerts.summary: The Sikkim High Court on September 22 directed the state to reconsider, within three weeks, its odd-even vehicle movement restriction on the NH-10 stretch from Mayfair Junction, Ranipool to Zero Point Junction, Gangtok; the case is listed for October 15. The restriction, introduced amid petrol/diesel buffer-stock concerns, was withdrawn for private vehicles outside Gangtok from May 31 but remains in force within Gangtok town.
alerts.impact: Until the policy changes, LM vehicles in Gangtok town can ply the Ranipool–Zero Point NH-10 stretch only on permitted days — plan alternate-day vehicle rostering (odd/even plates) for Gangtok hubs and keep two-wheeler riders on the core town beats; review again after the Oct 15 hearing.

alerts.title: Malappuram: Kottappuzha flash flood at TK Colony, Pookkottumpadam — one dead, seven feared missing
alerts.summary: A sudden flash flood in the Kottappuzha river struck TK Colony in Pookkottumpadam (Malappuram district, Nilambur belt) around 5 pm on September 20; one man was found dead at Muttikkund in Pottikkallu and seven people, including tourists, were feared swept away. About 27 people stranded mid-river were rescued; spots from Olarvattom Canal to TK Colony and the Koyipra foothills (Kettungal, Aanakkundu, Balawadippadi) were affected.
alerts.impact: Localised risk for Pookkottumpadam/Nilambur hill-foot LM routes during continuing Kerala orange-alert rain — avoid riverside village roads near Kottappuzha after heavy afternoon showers and allow SLA buffer for Nilambur-area pincodes.

alerts.title: Alluri Sitarama Raju: landslide at Chintalamma Ghat (Koyyuru mandal) drops debris on NH; Araku ghat landslips
alerts.summary: At Chintalamma Ghat Road in Koyyuru mandal of Alluri Sitarama Raju district, parts of the hillside gave way after heavy rain and earth and debris fell onto the National Highway, disrupting traffic on the ghat stretch. Araku Valley has had three days of continuous rain, with landslips reported along several ghat roads. Separately, flash floods hit several places in NTR district as streams and canals overflowed onto major roads, and hundreds of acres of paddy between Vijayawada and Rajahmundry are submerged.
alerts.impact: Avoid Chintalamma Ghat and Araku ghat roads for Vizag-Paderu/Araku feeder runs; move ASR-district LM to daylight-only with a 24-48h SLA buffer and flag Koyyuru, Paderu and Araku pincodes for extended TAT. Expect FM pickup misses in NTR district (Vijayawada rural) where flash floods have reached roads; heavy rain is forecast again on 25 September for NTR, Krishna, Guntur, Bapatla, Palnadu and Prakasam.

alerts.title: Kalahandi: red warning; landslide vigil at Madanpur Rampur, Koksara, Lanjigarh, Thuamul Rampur; Hati and Tel rising
alerts.summary: With IMD's red warning for extremely heavy rain over Kalahandi, Nabarangpur, Koraput and Malkangiri, the Kalahandi administration is maintaining strict vigilance in landslide-prone Madanpur Rampur, Koksara, Lanjigarh and Thuamul Rampur blocks. Continuous rain and gusty winds hit Dharmagada, Koksara and Jaipatna overnight, and the Hati and Tel rivers are steadily rising, prompting warnings to riverside residents. Schools and colleges in Kalahandi are closed; 28 temporary shelters and 13 mobile health units are ready.
alerts.impact: Early-warning item for Kalahandi: pre-flag Thuamul Rampur and Lanjigarh hill pincodes and Hati/Tel riverside villages (Dharmagada, Jaipatna, Koksara) for extended TAT on 24-26 September, and keep Bhawanipatna hub line-haul on main roads only. Escalate to non-serviceable if slides or river overtopping are reported.

alerts.title: Surat Ganesh Visarjan Sep 25: 25 main roads shut from 6 am; no heavy-vehicle entry from Palsana, Sayan, Olpad
alerts.summary: The Surat Police Commissioner's notification closes about 25 main roads, including the Rajmarg, to general traffic from 6 am on 25 September. Large idols will be immersed by crane at Hazira, Magdalla and Dumas; Dumas and Suvali beaches are closed to the public on 25-26 September, and air passengers are told to leave three hours early because of procession traffic on the Dumas route. All heavy vehicles entering Surat from Palsana, Sayan and Olpad are barred until immersion ends.
alerts.impact: Surat is a major Meesho supplier (textile) cluster - expect FM pickup failures across central Surat and the Dumas/Magdalla/Hazira belt on 25 September and hold line-haul trucks outside the city at Palsana/Kadodara until the no-entry lifts. Pull FM pickups forward to 24 September evening or push to 26 September, and route LM for western Surat (Piplod, Vesu, Dumas Road) as a next-day delivery.

alerts.title: Ahmedabad visarjan curbs from 1 pm Sep 25: Geeta Mandir-Jamalpur, Kalupur-Town Hall, Riverfront roads shut
alerts.summary: Ahmedabad Police Commissioner Anupamsinh Gehlot's notification, effective from 1 pm on 25 September, closes the ST Geeta Mandir-Jamalpur bridge-Paldi road, Geeta Mandir to Raipur/Sarangpur/Kalupur station, the Kalupur station-Sarangpur-Raipur-Khamasa-Ellisbridge-Town Hall stretch, Delhi Darwaja-Dadhichi bridge routes and the Riverfront road from Vadaj crematorium and Picnic House to under Ambedkar bridge. All restricted and diversion routes are no-parking zones; diversions run via Behrampura-Danilimda-Anjali and Kalupur bridge-Saraspur.
alerts.impact: Schedule Ahmedabad old-city and east-bank LM (Kalupur, Raipur, Jamalpur, Shahpur, Dariyapur) and FM pickups before 1 pm on 25 September; expect afternoon-evening failed attempts in walled-city pincodes and route line-haul to the Aslali/Changodar side via SP Ring Road rather than through the core.

alerts.title: Chhattisgarh: lightning kills 4 in Balod, Kanker, Bemetara; Bastar schools shut, Jagdalpur-Hyderabad flight cancelled
alerts.summary: Four people died in lightning strikes on Wednesday - a woman working in a field in Balod, a farmer in Kanker and two labourers near a pond in Bemetara. All schools in Bastar district were closed on 24 September and quarterly exams postponed, and the Jagdalpur-Hyderabad flight was cancelled due to weather. IMD has issued 40-60 km/h wind alerts for 14 districts including Raipur, Durg, Bilaspur, Kanker and Dhamtari, with heavy to very heavy rain possible in south Chhattisgarh on 24-25 September.
alerts.impact: Expect slower LM and FM in Bastar (Jagdalpur), Kanker and Kondagaon on 24-25 September and restrict rider movement in open rural stretches during thunderstorm windows; air-linked express loads into Jagdalpur should move by road via Raipur with a 1-day buffer.

alerts.title: Malkangiri: ghat landslide at Bayapada cuts off 18 villages; movement restricted both sides
alerts.summary: Deep-depression rain triggered a landslide on Thursday in the Bayapada area of Malkangiri district, where soil and debris from the ghat slid onto the road and cut off connectivity to 18 villages. Movement has been restricted on both sides of the ghat while the administration clears mud and stones; landslides at multiple other locations in Malkangiri were also reported. In neighbouring Rayagada, knee-deep water accumulated on roads and the Collector has flagged 11 landslide-prone hotspots.
alerts.impact: Treat Bayapada-ghat-dependent villages of Malkangiri as temporarily non-serviceable for LM until the road is cleared; hold FM pickups and route Malkangiri-bound loads with a 24-48h SLA buffer. Watch Rayagada's 11 flagged hotspots before dispatching line-haul through the ghats.

alerts.title: South Odisha: 237 villages in 6 districts hit, 8,082 shifted; bridges near Damjodi and Haridaphut under water
alerts.summary: Revenue Minister Suresh Pujari said 37 blocks, 160 gram panchayats and 237 villages plus 21 wards of 5 urban local bodies are affected across Koraput, Ganjam, Malkangiri, Gajapati, Nabarangpur and Rayagada; 8,082 people have been shifted and five senior officers sent to Malkangiri, Koraput, Nabarangpur, Gajapati and Kalahandi. In Koraput's Dasmantpur block, about three feet of water flowed over the bridge near Damjodi village (Nandigaon panchayat), stranding vehicles on both sides, and water also topped the bridge near Haridaphut (Pindapadar panchayat). Semiliguda recorded 230 mm and Jeypore 161 mm in 24 hours; 33 ODRAF teams are deployed. Updated 26 Sep: Revenue Minister Suresh Pujari said evacuations now stand at roughly 1,500 in Malkangiri, 4,000 in Nabarangpur and 7,000 in Gajapati (multiple landslides reported there); Baitarani river at Akhuapada is at 18.79m, above the 18.33m warning level. The minister said rainfall is expected to ease by 26 September evening with gradual improvement, but asked residents to stay alert for the next 24 hours.
alerts.impact: Expect LM failures and FM pickup misses across Koraput (Dasmantpur, Semiliguda, Jeypore), Malkangiri, Nabarangpur, Rayagada, Gajapati and Ganjam through the weekend — apply SLA relaxation, pre-emptively mark low-lying pincodes non-serviceable where bridges are overtopped, and avoid dispatching line-haul across submerged causeways. Situation is forecast to improve from the evening of 26 September — hold the SLA relaxation through Saturday and reassess Sunday before resuming normal LM/FM cadence in Malkangiri, Nabarangpur and Gajapati.

alerts.title: Keonjhar: water flowing over Panga and Sankarpur bridges in Telkoi, traffic hit
alerts.summary: Water is flowing over the Panga and Sankarpur bridges in Telkoi block of Keonjhar district, affecting traffic in the area, as the deep-depression rain spreads north from south Odisha. Telkoi's bridge crossings have repeatedly overtopped this monsoon, cutting links toward Jagamohanpur and NH-49.
alerts.impact: Hold LM vans for Telkoi-block villages beyond the Panga/Sankarpur crossings until water recedes; route Keonjhar-bound loads via NH-20/NH-49 main corridors and expect 1-day delay for Telkoi pincodes.

alerts.title: Andhra: 613 km of R&B roads damaged by deep depression, 356 km in Srikakulam alone; 4 washouts
alerts.summary: R&B Minister B.C. Janardhan Reddy said 613 km of state roads were damaged as of 7 a.m. Thursday, with Srikakulam accounting for 356 km. Roads were washed away at four locations by deep craters, cross-drainage works damaged at 78 locations (37 under restoration), and traffic disrupted at 23 locations (14 cleared). Damage is spread across Srikakulam, Parvathipuram-Manyam, Vizianagaram, Alluri Sitarama Raju, Visakhapatnam, Anakapalli, Kakinada, East Godavari, Konaseema, West Godavari, Anantapur, Kurnool and Nandyal.
alerts.impact: Srikakulam, Parvathipuram-Manyam and Vizianagaram LM should run on a 24-48h SLA buffer with alternate routing around washed-out stretches; watch Vizag hub outbound to north-coastal pincodes. 614 accident-prone spots have been flagged — avoid night line-haul on ghat and CD-damaged sections.

alerts.title: Vijayawada: continuous rain floods low-lying areas as deep depression moves inland
alerts.summary: After the deep depression crossed near Kalingapatnam between 11 pm Sep 23 and 1 am Sep 24, continuous rain since Thursday morning flooded low-lying areas of Vijayawada. IMD expects the system to hold deep-depression intensity for about 12 hours before weakening while moving north-northwest.
alerts.impact: Vijayawada city LM (low-lying colonies) may see failed attempts and slower first-attempt delivery today; keep Vijayawada/NTR district FM pickups flexible and watch for Krishna-district waterlogging spillover into Friday.

alerts.title: South Bengal: orange alert for 6 districts, up to 200 mm in Jhargram and Dum Dum; rain till Sep 27
alerts.summary: The remnant of the deep depression is bringing heavy to very heavy rain to East and West Midnapore and Jhargram, with heavy rain in South 24 Parganas, Bankura, Purulia, West Burdwan, Birbhum and Howrah; an orange alert is up for six districts and up to 200 mm is forecast in Dum Dum and Jhargram with 50-60 km/h winds. Kolkata recorded 65.4 mm in 24 hours and scattered rain is expected across south Bengal till Sunday, Sep 27. Evening update (25 Sep, Alipore Met Office): the system has now weakened into a regular depression after crossing the AP-Odisha coast; Kolkata, Howrah, Hooghly, North 24 Parganas, Jhargram, Purba Bardhaman, Nadia and Murshidabad continue to see scattered light-to-moderate rain, while Purba Medinipur, Paschim Medinipur and South 24 Parganas remain on orange alert for heavy rain and Purulia, Bankura, Paschim Bardhaman and Birbhum are on a separate heavy-rain alert through Saturday, 26 Sep.
alerts.impact: Plan for waterlogging-driven LM slowdowns in Kolkata/Dum Dum and rural Midnapore-Jhargram pincodes through Sep 27; avoid scheduling large FM pickups from Howrah/South 24 Parganas low-lying clusters during peak-rain windows and keep Durga Puja pre-festival volume buffers in mind.

alerts.title: Telangana: Jayashankar Bhupalpally drenched as deep depression rain washes away roads, submerges crops
alerts.summary: Telugu daily Andhra Jyothy reports heavy rain from the deep depression lashing Jayashankar Bhupalpally district, with floods washing away roads and submerging crops. Orange alerts covered 11 Telangana districts on Sep 23-24.
alerts.impact: Expect LM delays for interior Bhupalpally mandal pincodes and possible FM pickup gaps; route Bhupalpally-bound loads via main state highways only and add a 24h SLA buffer until road damage is assessed.

alerts.title: Raipur Ganesh Visarjan from Sep 25, jhanki procession Sep 27: police traffic and safety rules
alerts.summary: Raipur police have issued traffic and safety rules for Ganesh idol immersion starting September 25, with the main jhanki procession on September 27, and heavy vehicles are banned on 19 city routes until September 27 under the revised festival traffic plan. This coincides with IMD's forecast of widespread rain over Chhattisgarh through Sep 29 and 40-60 km/h wind alerts for Raipur and 14 other districts.
alerts.impact: Schedule Raipur city LM and FM runs outside procession hours on Sep 25-27, expect heavy-vehicle diversions on procession routes, and plan for rain-plus-procession delays in central Raipur pincodes.

alerts.title: TSPC calls 3-day bandh Sep 24-26 in Chatra, Hazaribagh, Palamu, Latehar, Garhwa, Lohardaga, Gumla
alerts.summary: The Maoist splinter group TSPC (Tritiya Prastuti Committee) has called a three-day shutdown from 24 to 26 September across seven Jharkhand districts - Chatra, Hazaribagh, Palamu, Latehar, Garhwa, Lohardaga and Gumla - calling the police encounter of its leader Brijesh Ganjhu in Uttar Pradesh fake. Posters announcing the bandh have been put up, and the districts are on alert for three days.
alerts.impact: Naxal-called bandhs in this belt typically halt trucks and rural road traffic even where markets open - hold line-haul into Palamu (Daltonganj), Latehar, Garhwa and Chatra for 24-26 September and push FM pickups to 27 September. Expect LM attempt failures in rural pincodes of all seven districts; Hazaribagh town and Ranchi-bound NH traffic may run with security escort only.

alerts.title: Srikakulam: Vamsadhara and Nagavali in spate; culvert at Gangavaram washed away, 53 riverside villages on alert
alerts.summary: The Vamsadhara and Nagavali rivers in Srikakulam district are in spate with heavy inflows after the deep depression's landfall. A canal culvert at Gangavaram village was washed away, cutting road links to several villages, and precautionary measures are in place in 53 villages in the river basin. The district red alert continues, with cyclone-impact risk flagged in ten coastal mandals; rainwater entered homes at Bhavani Nagar in Tekkali and a tree fell in Neelapuram mandal.
alerts.impact: Flag villages beyond the Gangavaram culvert and low-lying Vamsadhara-Nagavali basin pincodes as non-serviceable until the road is restored. Hold Srikakulam and Tekkali LM for 24-25 September and reroute via NH-16 only once waters drop.

alerts.title: Odisha: huge rock blocks Paribeta Ghat road in Gajapati's R. Udayagiri block; 1,500 evacuated statewide
alerts.summary: Incessant rain triggered a landslide on the Paribeta Ghat road in R. Udayagiri block of Gajapati district, where a huge rock tumbled onto the road and disrupted traffic; no injuries were reported. Gajapati has identified 140 landslide-vulnerable spots. Across south Odisha, falling trees and road blockades have been reported from Gajapati and Ganjam, with about 1,500 people evacuated and rainfall of around 230 mm recorded.
alerts.impact: Treat R. Udayagiri and Mohana-side Gajapati pincodes as extended-TAT until the ghat is cleared; avoid Paribeta Ghat for Berhampur-Paralakhemundi feeder runs. Keep Ganjam and Gajapati FM pickups on hold for 24 September.

alerts.title: Assam: Brahmaputra within 10 m of breaching Biswanath Ghat-Panpur embankment at Solmari village
alerts.summary: Strong Brahmaputra currents have eaten about 200 metres of land at Solmari village, bringing the river to within 10 metres of the Biswanath Ghat-Panpur embankment. The stretch had been safe since anti-erosion works in 2014. Locals have urged the administration to deploy mega geo-bags immediately, warning the embankment could breach if erosion continues at the current rate.
alerts.impact: Early-warning item for Biswanath district: an embankment breach would flood Biswanath Ghat and Panpur-side villages. Keep Biswanath Chariali LM on normal SLA but pre-flag riverside pincodes for extended TAT, and watch for breach reports before dispatch.

alerts.title: Hyderabad Ganesh Nimajjanam Sep 25: curbs on Upper Tank Bund, PVNR and NTR Marg; Cyberabad diversions
alerts.summary: Hyderabad's main Ganesh immersion is on 25 September. Immersion from Tank Bund is prohibited following court directions, with idols routed to NTR Gardens, People's Plaza, Necklace Road and artificial ponds. Traffic will tighten around Hussain Sagar with need-based restrictions on PVNR Marg and NTR Marg and movement curbs on Upper Tank Bund, with about 1,200 traffic personnel deployed; Cyberabad police have separately notified traffic curbs. More than 43,000 idols had already been immersed ahead of the main day.
alerts.impact: Treat central Hyderabad (Khairatabad, Himayatnagar, Secunderabad, Lakdikapul) as a no-movement zone from the afternoon of 25 September to the early hours of 26 September, compounded by the ongoing rain alert. Move Hyderabad city FM pickups to the morning of the 25th and route line-haul via the Outer Ring Road.

alerts.title: 644 trucks and oil tankers stranded at Jiribam after Awangkhul and Nungba landslides cut NH-37
alerts.summary: Landslides at Awangkhul and Nungba in Noney district cut the Imphal-Jiribam section of NH-37, leaving 644 goods trucks stranded at Jiribam - oil tankers, foodgrain carriers and construction-material vehicles. Separately reported counts put around 800 goods trucks and fuel tankers stuck across Manipur and Assam, with a security-escort shortage compounding the landslide closures. No clearance report has surfaced.
alerts.impact: NH-37 is the Silchar lifeline into Imphal and it is both slide-blocked and blockade-bound - do not dispatch Manipur-bound line-haul via Jiribam. Assume Imphal, Thoubal, Bishnupur and Churachandpur stay on extended TAT or non-serviceable until both the slides and the UNC blockade clear.

alerts.title: Himachal ends monsoon with 47 roads still blocked - Mandi 21, Kangra 10, Kullu 7
alerts.summary: Himachal's State Emergency Operations Centre listed 47 roads still blocked statewide on 22 September - Mandi 21, Kangra 10, Kullu 7, Sirmaur and Una 3 each, Lahaul-Spiti 2 and Shimla 1. The count has fallen steadily from 60 on 18 September, so the network is slowly recovering. The 85-day monsoon window from 30 June to 22 September closed with 354 deaths and damage above Rs 3,219 crore, with 601 houses fully destroyed and 1,416 partially damaged.
alerts.impact: Mandi and Kullu remain the binding constraint on Himachal hill line-haul - keep relaxed SLAs on Mandi, Kullu and Kangra rural pincodes but begin restoring normal cut-offs as the blocked count falls. Rebuild FM pickup slots into Kangra first, where the road count is improving fastest.

alerts.title: Himachal Pradesh: Manikaran-Barshaini road (Parvati Valley, Kullu) still not confirmed cleared — repeat slides at Ghatigad keep damaging vehicles
alerts.summary: A large landslide blocked the Manikaran-Barshaini road in Kullu district's Parvati Valley, stranding travellers and cutting connectivity to upper-valley villages including Kasol and Barshaini. The stretch remains volatile — a subsequent slide at Ghatigad damaged another car days later — and no source confirms full restoration as of Sep 22.
alerts.impact: Flag Parvati Valley (Manikaran-Barshaini-Kasol) pincodes non-serviceable for LM/FM until the road is confirmed cleared; route via alternate Kullu-valley approaches where available.

alerts.title: J&K: Doda-Bhaderwah road still blocked at Chalnai village after Sep 19 landslide, no reopening confirmed
alerts.summary: The Doda-Bhaderwah road remains blocked near Chalnai village after a landslide on September 19 halted vehicular movement between the two towns. Debris-clearance machinery remains engaged, but no source confirms full restoration as of Sep 22 — treat the road as still disrupted.
alerts.impact: Route watch — Doda-Bhaderwah corridor: hold non-essential LM/linehaul via Chalnai until the road is confirmed cleared, and route via alternate approach roads where available for Bhaderwah-side pincodes.

alerts.title: NH-44 Jammu-Srinagar open but slow: single-lane chokepoints at Dhalwal and Marog-Nachil Pather
alerts.summary: The 23 September J&K traffic advisory shows NH-44 flowing rather than closed, with very slow movement over a 30-40 metre single-lane stretch of uneven surface at Dhalwal in Udhampur and the single-lane Marog-Nachil Pather section. Vehicle breakdowns between Nashri and Ramsoo and the movement of nomadic herds from Marog to Kishtwar Pather added further delays. Oil and gas tankers remain restricted on the Digdo-Khooni Nallah stretch between 0700 and 1900 hrs, and are allowed beyond Chenani only between 1700 and 0500 hrs.
alerts.impact: Downgrade Jammu-Srinagar from blocked to regulated: plan Kashmir Valley line-haul on daylight-only LMV runs and add roughly half a day of buffer on Srinagar, Anantnag and Baramulla inbound. Fuel and LPG resupply to Valley hubs must be scheduled around the Digdo-Khooni Nallah tanker window.

alerts.title: J&K: LeT logistics module busted in Rajouri's Chassana/Reasi-Shopian belt — network described as contained, probe widening
alerts.summary: Police confirmed three OGWs arrested (Sep 15-19) facilitated terrorist movement across the Rajouri-Reasi-Shopian belt, linked to the 2023 Chassana encounter; a pistol, grenades and an IED were recovered. The immediate cell is described as neutralized, though the wider probe continues. No curfews, checkpoints or transport restrictions have resulted from this case as of Sep 22.
alerts.impact: Watch item — Rajouri/Reasi/Shopian/Poonch belt pincodes: monitor for any follow-on movement restrictions or network curbs; no current LM/FM action needed but keep contingency routing in mind for this corridor.

alerts.title: J&K: ISI spy network arrest in Kathua — accused installed SIM-enabled CCTV to feed live army-route footage to Pakistan
alerts.summary: Police in Kathua arrested Mohd Aman on Sep 21 for allegedly installing SIM-enabled CCTV cameras to transmit live army-movement footage to Pakistan — a case distinct from the Rajouri LeT module. No transport or movement restrictions have followed as of Sep 22.
alerts.impact: Watch item only — no current LM/FM restriction in the Kathua belt; monitor for any follow-on security cordon that could affect border-district routing.

alerts.title: Pithoragarh-Tanakpur NH-9 night traffic banned 6pm-6am at Ghat Bend until roughly 2 October
alerts.summary: Continuous shooting stones and debris from a vulnerable slope near Ghat Bend on the Pithoragarh-Tanakpur all-weather road (NH-9) have caused repeated blockages and injured passengers in commercial vehicles. Pithoragarh district administration ordered vehicles not to ply between 6 pm and 6 am for at least 15 days from around 17 September, so the night curfew runs to roughly 2 October. NH officials will permanently treat the slope across a 200-metre width, up from the 100 metres treated earlier.
alerts.impact: Kumaon line-haul into Pithoragarh, Dharchula and Munsiyari loses its night window until about 2 October - re-cut departures from Tanakpur and Khatima to arrive before 6 pm or accept a day's slip. Flag Pithoragarh-district rural pincodes for extended TAT rather than non-serviceable.

alerts.title: UP floods: 12 villages under water in Gonda's Tarabganj & Karnalganj, 54 in Varanasi, 45 in Gorakhpur
alerts.summary: Floods now span 23 of Uttar Pradesh's districts with over 16,000 people evacuated. In Gonda district the Ghaghra and Sarayu have crossed danger level in Tarabganj and Karnalganj tehsils, submerging 12 villages. Rising Ganga, Varuna, Gomti and Nand waters have flooded 54 villages in Varanasi, and the Rapti and Sarayu have partly or fully submerged 45 villages in Gorakhpur. Sharda, Ganga and Sarayu levels continue to rise, cutting road links and prompting relocation advisories in low-lying areas.
alerts.impact: Flag rural pincodes in Gonda (Tarabganj, Karnalganj), Varanasi rural, Gorakhpur, Ballia, Lakhimpur Kheri and Bahraich as non-serviceable or extended-SLA until waters recede. Route Purvanchal line-haul via NH-27 and Lucknow rather than riverine district roads, and rebalance FM pickup capacity from flooded blocks to the Lucknow and Kanpur hubs.

alerts.title: Brent slips below $100 to ~$98 on Iran's Hormuz reopening offer; pump prices unchanged, commercial LPG Rs 2,747.50
alerts.summary: Oil fell about 3% after Iran offered to reopen the Strait of Hormuz within seven days if the US eases pressure, taking Brent below $100 to around $98 a barrel and WTI to about $91. Indian pump prices have not yet moved. Brent crude is trading near $102 a barrel amid Strait of Hormuz shipping disruption. Pump prices held steady again on 23 September: Delhi petrol Rs 102.12 and diesel Rs 95.20, Mumbai Rs 111.21 and Rs 97.83, Chennai Rs 107.76 and Rs 99.55, Bengaluru Rs 110.82 and Rs 98.78, and Hyderabad Rs 115.69 and Rs 103.82 - the costliest metro for both fuels. The 19-kg commercial LPG cylinder is at Rs 2,747.50 in Delhi, up Rs 669 (32.2%) since April, and Rs 2,831.00 in Bengaluru; domestic 14.2-kg LPG is Rs 942 in Delhi. CNG stands at Rs 86.98/kg in Delhi, Rs 88 in Mumbai, Rs 97 in Bengaluru, Rs 112 in Hyderabad, Rs 97.50 in Chennai, Rs 94.02 in Ahmedabad and Rs 93.50 in Kolkata.
alerts.impact: Diesel above Rs 95 in Delhi and above Rs 103 in Hyderabad, with crude over $100, keeps upward pressure on 3P per-shipment LM/FM rates - expect Delhivery, Shadowfax and Xpressbees to raise fuel-surcharge asks in the next rate cycle. Hyderabad is now the worst metro on both diesel (Rs 103.82) and CNG (Rs 112/kg), which materially worsens LM economics there versus Delhi and Mumbai; factor this into capacity-expansion cost cases for Telangana pincodes.

alerts.title: Mumbai bars heavy vehicles 11am-1pm on 23 and 25 September; visarjan curbs from 10am on the 25th
alerts.summary: Mumbai bans all categories of heavy vehicles and private buses from 11 am to 1 pm on 20, 23 and 25 September everywhere except South Mumbai, which has its own ban on 21, 24, 26 and 29 September. Heavy vehicles are restricted on the Jogeshwari-Vikhroli Link Road from 10:00 on 25 September to 12:00 on 26 September. Citywide immersion restrictions run from 10 am on 25 September until each procession concludes. BMC has readied over 383 artificial ponds and 67 natural immersion sites with more than 25,000 personnel, and Navi Mumbai police have notified separate curbs across Vashi and Panvel. Vasai, Nalasopara and Naigaon add a heavy-vehicle ban from 2 pm to midnight.
alerts.impact: Anant Chaturdashi on 25 September is the hardest LM/FM stoppage of the month for Mumbai and Navi Mumbai - treat 25 September afternoon to night as a no-movement window and shift Bhiwandi and Panvel line-haul to pre-dawn on the 25th or after noon on the 26th. Do not commit same-day promises in Mumbai, Thane, Vasai-Virar or Navi Mumbai for 25 September.

alerts.title: Raghuveer Ghat still not open at full capacity; Khed-Satara link under repair and wall work
alerts.summary: Tarun Bharat reports Raghuveer Ghat, the Khed (Ratnagiri) to Satara link, has still not been restored to full traffic capacity, with PWD road repair and protective retaining-wall construction running on a war footing. This follows the early-September landslide in which part of the carriageway caved after cloudburst-like rain, halting two-way traffic, severing 15-20 Satara-side villages and stranding an ST bus. The ghat stays degraded going into the 23-25 September yellow alert that explicitly covers Ratnagiri and Satara Ghat.
alerts.impact: Do not plan Ratnagiri-Satara cross-ghat middle-mile on Raghuveer until a reopening is confirmed; route via Kumbharli or Amba Ghat instead. The 15-20 cut-off Satara-side villages should stay flagged for extended TAT rather than serviceable.

alerts.title: Maharashtra yellow alert for 33 locations on Sep 23; Nanded, Latur, Dharashiv flagged, ~49 roads shut in Latur
alerts.summary: IMD has issued a yellow alert for 33 locations across Maharashtra for 23 September, with heavy rain, thunderstorms and lightning expected in Marathwada. Nanded, Latur and Dharashiv may see isolated heavy showers with strong winds, and all Marathwada districts are under yellow alert. Rising river and stream levels have submerged roads and bridges, with close to 49 roads shut in Latur district. Extreme rainfall between August and September has damaged crops across roughly 6.9 million acres in 30 districts, with Nanded, Beed, Solapur, Yavatmal and Buldhana worst hit.
alerts.impact: Expect continued LM attempt failure and FM pickup loss across Nanded, Latur, Dharashiv, Beed and Parbhani rural pincodes; roughly 49 closed roads in Latur make several interior blocks effectively non-serviceable. Route Marathwada line-haul via Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar and avoid causeway-dependent village routes. Rural buyer demand may also soften on crop loss - size Marathwada capacity conservatively.

alerts.title: Kerala eases to yellow alert in 7 districts Sep 23-25 after flash floods killed 9 in Malappuram, Kottayam, Idukki
alerts.summary: IMD has an orange alert running for Kottayam, Idukki, Ernakulam, Thrissur, Malappuram and Palakkad with winds up to 40 kmph, and isolated heavy rain forecast for Kerala from 20 to 24 September. Flash floods and landslides have killed nine people in 24 hours - five in Malappuram and two each in Kottayam and Idukki - with several still missing. IMD scientist Neetha K Gopal has flagged cloudburst potential and landslide risk on the Idukki-Wayanad ghats. Authorities have advised against night travel in hilly areas and the Meenachil river is swollen at Kottayam. IMD has since scaled the outlook to isolated heavy rain from 23 to 25 September, with Thiruvananthapuram, Kollam, Pathanamthitta, Kottayam, Idukki, Kannur and Kasaragod under yellow alert.
alerts.impact: Keep night line-haul off the Idukki-Wayanad ghat sections and the Kottayam-Kumily and Thodupuzha routes. Treat Malappuram, Kottayam and Idukki hill pincodes as extended-SLA and expect Ernakulam and Thrissur LM attempt failure from waterlogging. Stage buffer stock at Kochi rather than upcountry hill hubs until 25 Sep.

alerts.title: Karnataka: Agumbe Ghat (NH-169A) heavy-vehicle ban stays in force through September 30 on landslide risk
alerts.summary: Movement of heavy vehicles through Agumbe Ghat on NH-169A, the Malpe-Thirthahalli link, remains prohibited until 30 September because of landslide risk from continuous heavy rain, a ban that has run since 15 June. Only light motor vehicles are permitted. Heavy vehicles from Thirthahalli towards Udupi are directed via the Thirthahalli-Nagar-Kundapur-Udupi route. The 24 September red alert for Dakshina Kannada and Udupi makes an extension beyond 30 September likely.
alerts.impact: Route all Udupi and Mangaluru-bound heavy vehicles via Thirthahalli-Nagar-Kundapur and price the extra leg into Malnad middle-mile costs through at least 30 September. With Agumbe shut, Shiradi and Charmadi carry the entire Bengaluru-Mangaluru load and a slide on either is a single point of failure.

alerts.title: Red alert for Dakshina Kannada & Udupi on Sep 24; orange for Shivamogga, Chikkamagaluru, Kalaburagi, Vijayapura
alerts.summary: IMD has placed Kalaburagi, Vijayapura, Udupi, Shivamogga, Chikkamagaluru and Dakshina Kannada under an orange alert for heavy to very heavy rain on 23 September, escalating to a red alert for Dakshina Kannada and Udupi on 24 September for extremely heavy rainfall. Yellow alerts cover Bidar, Yadgir, Raichur, Bagalkote, Vijayanagara, Uttara Kannada, Chitradurga and Hassan. Schools have been shut in parts of Shivamogga and Chikkamagaluru.
alerts.impact: Coastal Karnataka LM (Mangaluru, Udupi, Kundapura, Karkala) should plan for a near-washout on 24 Sep - pull FM pickups forward to 23 Sep morning and hold Mangaluru-bound line-haul. Malnad ghat pincodes around Agumbe, Sringeri, Shivamogga and Chikkamagaluru stay at high non-adherence risk; keep Kalaburagi and Vijayapura on watch for localised waterlogging.

sources.name: Karnataka rain alert - red alert for Shivamogga & Chikkamagaluru, schools shut (ground report, TV)

alerts.title: Telangana red alert extended through Sat 26 Sep for Asifabad, Mancherial, Bhupalpally, Mulugu and Bhadradri Kothagudem
alerts.summary: The Hyderabad Met Centre issued a red alert for Komaram Bheem Asifabad, Mancherial, Jayashankar Bhupalpally, Mulugu and Bhadradri Kothagudem for Thursday to Saturday (24-26 Sep), with an orange alert for Adilabad, Jagtial, Karimnagar, Peddapalli, Khammam, Mahabubabad, Warangal and Hanamkonda; winds up to 65 kmph and lightning expected. Revenue Minister Ponguleti Srinivas Reddy told collectors to stay on 24x7 alert and set up control rooms; Bhadradri Kothagudem schools were shut on 23-24 Sep.
alerts.impact: Hold non-urgent LM dispatch to agency mandals of Mulugu, Bhupalpally and Kothagudem (Godavari belt) till 26 Sep; expect FM pickup misses from Mancherial/Asifabad sellers. Hyderabad itself is only under yellow alert, but 25 Sep is also a Ganesh-immersion holiday there.

alerts.title: Tamil Nadu: fishermen advised off Gulf of Mannar and Comorin Sea as squally winds up to 55 kmph forecast
alerts.summary: Squally winds of 45-55 kmph gusting occasionally to 65 kmph are forecast over the Gulf of Mannar, the adjoining Comorin area and the south Tamil Nadu coast. Permits are not being issued to mechanised boat fishermen at Rameswaram, and the restriction remains in force until further notice as a precaution against rough seas. No withdrawal of the advisory has been reported.
alerts.impact: Ramanathapuram and Thoothukudi coastal FM volume tied to fishing-harbour clusters stays suppressed while permits are withheld. Keep Rameswaram-island pincodes on extended TAT and avoid committing same-day there.

alerts.title: Odisha: villages remain marooned in Sundargarh's Bonai block as Sarasara, Patang bridges near Balang stay submerged
alerts.summary: At least five villages remain marooned in Sundargarh district's Bonai block after the Sarasara and Patang bridges near Balang stayed submerged; no confirmation of bridge clearance has surfaced. Pre-build buffer stock at Rourkela hub given the compounding cyclone landfall expected Sep 23-24.
alerts.impact: Flag Bonai block villages non-serviceable until bridges are confirmed clear; pre-build buffer stock at Rourkela hub given the compounding cyclone landfall on Sep 23-24.

alerts.title: NH-326 bridges submerged 4 ft in Malkangiri — Malkangiri–Kalimela/Matu and Kalimela–Padia traffic halted, bridges closed
alerts.summary: Several bridges on National Highway 326 in Malkangiri were submerged with water flowing about four feet above, halting transport between Malkangiri and Kalimela/Matu and between Kalimela and Padia. Hundreds of vehicles were stranded on both sides and the district administration ordered temporary closure of the bridges; Chitrakonda (168 mm), Kalimela (127 mm) and Malkangiri town (101 mm) were among the wettest stations.
alerts.impact: Kalimela, Motu, Padia and Chitrakonda-area pincodes are effectively non-serviceable from Malkangiri hub until NH-326 bridges reopen; hold dispatch and flag orders for extended SLA. Linehaul to Malkangiri via Jeypore should wait for the district's bridge-reopening advisory.

alerts.title: Jharkhand yellow alert for 11 districts on 23 September, orange for five districts on 24 September
alerts.summary: IMD has a yellow alert on 23 September for Lohardaga, Gumla, Simdega, Ramgarh, Ranchi, Khunti, Bokaro, Dhanbad, Saraikela-Kharsawan and East and West Singhbhum, with an orange alert following on 24 September for five districts. Heavy to very heavy rain is flagged across Gumla, Simdega, Ranchi, Khunti, West Singhbhum, Latehar, Lohardaga, Ramgarh, Hazaribagh, Koderma, Giridih, Bokaro, Dhanbad and Saraikela-Kharsawan, with rain continuing to 26 September. Peak impact is expected on 24 September, driven by the same Bay of Bengal system.
alerts.impact: Ranchi, Jamshedpur and Dhanbad hub outbound should carry a day's buffer for 24 September, with Gumla, Simdega, Khunti and West Singhbhum rural pincodes the most exposed. Keep Ranchi FM pickup slots in the morning window ahead of the afternoon peak.

alerts.title: Jharkhand: Ganga flood in Sahibganj floods Bhartiya Colony, Rasoolpur; Udhwa erosion sweeps away school and homes
alerts.summary: The Ganga is flowing roughly 57cm above the danger mark at Sahibganj, flooding Bhartiya Colony and Rasoolpur localities; separately, erosion in Udhwa block has destroyed homes and a school building in the Ganga diyara belt.
alerts.impact: Flag Sahibganj town (Bhartiya Colony, Rasoolpur) and Udhwa diyara-belt pincodes non-serviceable; verify riverside addresses before LM dispatch and monitor for further erosion through the week.

alerts.title: Padma erosion swallows 19 houses and a Manasa temple at Radhakrishnapur, Taranagar in Raghunathganj II
alerts.summary: Erosion turned severe in the Radhakrishnapur area of Taranagar village in Raghunathganj II block, Murshidabad, taking 19 homes, an old Manasa temple, shops and several bighas of farmland. Another 50 to 70 houses are under immediate threat. The Farakka-belt blocks - Farakka, Samserganj, Suti I and II, Raghunathganj II, Lalgola, Bhagawangola I and II, Raninagar I and II and Jalangi - face this every year.
alerts.impact: Treat Raghunathganj II, Suti and Samserganj riverside pincodes as shrinking serviceable areas and re-verify addresses before dispatch. Route Murshidabad FM through Jangipur town rather than the riverbank villages.

alerts.title: Fresh Ganga erosion in Malda's Manikchak washes away about 50 houses; nine schools suspend classes
alerts.summary: Fresh Ganga erosion in the Manikchak block of Malda washed away around 50 houses and triggered panic among residents. The district administration suspended classes at nine primary schools across the Manikchak and Ratua-I blocks. Irrigation engineers expect erosion to continue to the end of September because of fluctuating Ganga levels, and state ministers inspected flood and erosion-hit stretches in Manikchak and Ratua-I on 19 September.
alerts.impact: Manikchak and Ratua-I pincodes need address re-validation as households relocate, and FM pickup from riverside seller clusters there should be suspended rather than reattempted. Expect continued serviceability loss across Malda through end-September.

alerts.title: North Bengal flagged for 7-11 cm on 23-24 September; LC-3 hoisted at Kolkata and Haldia ports
alerts.summary: RMC Kolkata's 22 September bulletin puts light to moderate rain over all North Bengal districts on 23-24 September with heavy rain of 7-11 cm at one or two places over Jalpaiguri and Darjeeling. Widespread rain is forecast for Sub-Himalayan West Bengal and Sikkim from 22 to 26 September and for Gangetic West Bengal from 20 to 26 September. Local Cautionary Signal No. 3 is hoisted at Kolkata and Haldia ports with Sectional Signal No. 1 at Sagar Island, and fishermen are barred from the sea off West Bengal from 22 to 25 September.
alerts.impact: This is the precursor window for fresh Darjeeling, Kalimpong and NH-10 slides - keep Siliguri buffer stock high and treat hill pincodes as at-risk from 23 September. Kolkata and Haldia port-linked inbound should assume degraded throughput for 23-25 September.

alerts.title: NH-10 at Bardang 20th Mile back to one-way traffic after 17 September mudslide
alerts.summary: A mudslide blocked NH-10 at Bardang, 20th Mile on the morning of 17 September, suspending movement. The stretch reopened to one-way traffic on 20 September after a day-long clearance in dry weather; twelve households were affected, Rs 2,70,400 in relief was distributed and one person was injured. Boulders and sludge at the site remain a live concern and the Sikkim chief secretary has directed early full reopening. IMD forecasts 7-11 cm at one or two places over Darjeeling and Jalpaiguri on 23-24 September, the classic precursor for fresh NH-10 slides. NH-10 at 20th Mile, Bardang was reopened to one-way traffic on 20 September after a day-long clearance, and the 30th Mile stretch was also temporarily opened, but the section remains soft and waterlogged and drivers are advised to go slow.
alerts.impact: Siliguri-Gangtok line-haul is running but single-lane, so plan one-way convoy timings and roughly half a day of extra transit. With heavy rain forecast for 23-24 September, hold a contingency for full NH-10 closure and keep Gangtok buffer stock topped up.

alerts.title: Brahmaputra erosion devours Majuli's Bhakat Chapari and Chabua's Balijan; 25 families homeless
alerts.summary: Massive erosion is under way along Bhakat Chapari in Majuli, with the threat now extending to 16 villages and lower Majuli. At Balijan in Chabua a single day's erosion washed away crores' worth of geo-bags and at least 25 families lost homes and farmland. The Water Resources Department is dumping sand-filled geo-bags from boats. Over the decade to 2026, 330 Assam villages have been lost and 23,369 families displaced by erosion, with the Brahmaputra widening 4.64 km at Dhubri.
alerts.impact: Majuli and Chabua address bases are physically shifting - re-validate Majuli, Chabua and Dhubri pincode masters against relocated households before pushing volume, or non-delivery will read as rider failure rather than address loss. Keep Majuli on extended TAT and treat lower-Majuli villages as at risk of permanent serviceability loss.

alerts.title: Rimbi village landslide worsens: 35 houses damaged, Singlitam hillock still active, both approach roads shut
alerts.summary: A recurring mudslide that began on 12 September at the Singlitam hillock above Rimbi village (West Sikkim, Yuksom-Tashiding constituency) intensified further after Yuksom-Rimbi recorded 224.6mm of rain in 24 hours - the highest in Sikkim. Ground reports on 25 September put the toll at 35 houses damaged (no casualties); the Rimbi-Yuksom and Rimbi-Khecheopalri roads remain closed, and the Geyzing district administration is running relief camps at Rimbi Panchayat Bhawan for evacuated families.
alerts.impact: Treat Rimbi, Yuksom and Khecheopalri (Geyzing subdivision, West Sikkim) as non-serviceable for LM/FM until both roads reopen; hold any COD/RTO pickups in the area and re-route West Sikkim linehaul via alternate roads with a 3-4 day SLA buffer given the slope is still active. Flag Pelling-belt sellers for pickup delays.

alerts.title: Manipur: Joint Tribes Council backs UNC indefinite blockade on NH-2, NH-202, NH-37, NH-102A; 100+ trucks stranded
alerts.summary: The United Naga Council's indefinite inter-district economic blockade, in force since 1 am on 9 September, has been intensified on NH-2, NH-202 (Jessami), NH-37 (Jiribam) and NH-102A (Tadubi-Ukhrul). Goods-laden vehicles are barred on these highways, with exemptions only for medical supplies, media, power, telecom and water-supply vehicles. More than 100 goods trucks and fuel tankers carrying essential commodities are stranded in Senapati and the Tamenglong-Noney belt. The Joint Tribes Council Manipur has endorsed the blockade and appealed for strict compliance. The UNC is demanding accountability for the killing of six Naga civilians at Leilon Vaiphei in Kangpokpi on 13 May 2026 and the removal of Deputy CM Nemcha Kipgen.
alerts.impact: Imphal valley remains effectively cut off for commercial freight - keep Manipur pincodes flagged non-serviceable and do not commit new LM capacity there. Trucks held at Senapati and in the Tamenglong-Noney belt should be re-routed or recalled to Dimapur or Guwahati rather than left idling. Plan Northeast fill-rate recovery through the Guwahati and Silchar hubs only.

alerts.title: Haryana rice millers boycott CMR registration before 1 October procurement; 6.5 lakh MT stuck
alerts.summary: Around 6.5 lakh MT of custom-milled rice worth nearly Rs 2,800 crore is lying in Haryana mills because FCI has not accepted it, and only about 350 of nearly 1,400 millers have registered for the 2026-27 season starting 1 October. Millers have announced a boycott of CMR operations and want pending milling, holding, blending and transportation charges cleared. The Centre extended the CMR delivery deadline to 30 September but FCI has restricted officials from accepting further stock.
alerts.impact: A stalled 1 October kharif procurement would free up rather than consume Haryana truck capacity, easing Karnal, Kaithal and Kurukshetra hire rates in early October. Watch for the opposite case too - a last-minute settlement that pulls every available trailer into mandi movement just as Navratri volume ramps.

alerts.title: Sharda river erosion swallows nine houses in Lakhimpur Kheri; 20 more at risk, villagers self-demolishing
alerts.summary: Nine houses have been lost to Sharda river erosion in Lakhimpur Kheri with 20 more in immediate danger, and villagers are demolishing their own homes to salvage bricks; the Virbaba Sthan site is also threatened. Earlier in the season the Sharda ran 32 cm above the danger mark after 1.91 lakh cusecs were released from Banbasa barrage, pushing water into villages of the Palia, Bhira and Bijua blocks where residents needed boats to move. Sharda-Mohana erosion is reported intensifying across three separate pockets of the district. As of 24 September, erosion has intensified further along the Mohana-Sharda confluence stretch, with standing crops now also at risk in addition to homes.
alerts.impact: Palia, Bhira and Bijua block pincodes need address re-validation and should stay on extended TAT - households are moving, so non-delivery there is address loss, not rider failure. Hold FM pickup from riverside seller clusters until the Banbasa release stabilises.

alerts.title: NH-66 Mumbai-Goa bars 16-tonne-plus trucks and trailers through the 26 September festival window
alerts.summary: Maharashtra banned multi-axle trucks, trailers and heavy goods carriers of 16 tonnes and above on NH-66 across the Ganeshotsav travel and immersion windows from 11 to 26 September, including a hard 39-hour block from 08:00 on 19 September to 23:00 on 20 September that has now elapsed. The state subsequently revised the order to let police relax restrictions where conditions permit. Milk, petrol, diesel, domestic LPG cylinders, medicines, ambulances, police and fire vehicles are exempt.
alerts.impact: The Mumbai-Goa trunk is closed to full-truck-load movement until 26 September - run Konkan and Goa replenishment on sub-16T vehicles or hold to the 27th. Combine this with the Raghuveer Ghat restriction when planning Ratnagiri and Sindhudurg FM coverage.

alerts.title: Pune bars heavy vehicles from 12 central roads including Laxmi, Tilak, Bajirao and Karve to 26 September
alerts.summary: Pune has barred heavy and oversized vehicles from 12 key central roads - Laxmi Road, Tilak Road, Bajirao Road and Karve Road among them - from 12 to 26 September. Parts of Laxmi Road, Shivaji Road and Bajirao Road are closed round the clock and several other roads shut to vehicles every evening from 5 pm. Separate diversions were notified for Wagholi on 22 September. PMPML is running 799 extra buses through 25 September with services to 2 am.
alerts.impact: Pune's city core - Sadashiv Peth, Shukrawar Peth, Narayan Peth and Budhwar Peth pincodes - is effectively two-wheeler-only until 26 September, so reroute van-based LM to the Wagholi, Hadapsar and Kothrud edges and pull evening cut-offs ahead of 5 pm.

alerts.title: Nhava Sheva/JNPA congestion persists; gate-in turnaround near 20 hours for some truckers
alerts.summary: JNPT/Nhava Sheva continues to run congested on vessel bunching, terminal capacity pressure, rail delays and equipment shortage, compounded by spillover from disruptions at neighbouring private ports and tighter festival road restrictions. Gate-in turnaround has stretched to roughly 20 hours for some truckers, with slow import-container evacuation and driver shortages. Shippers are being advised to book at least a week ahead.
alerts.impact: Import-dependent inbound into Bhiwandi and Panvel should assume a week's booking lead and an extra day of dwell - do not commit tight inbound receipt dates through end-September. This compounds with the NH-66 16T ban and the Mumbai visarjan vehicle curbs on the same corridor.

alerts.title: Marathwada drought protests: Dharashiv farmers block the Dhule-Solapur highway at Yedshi
alerts.summary: Marathwada is running a 38% rainfall shortfall with a near six-week dry spell that has scorched soybean and cotton. Farmers in Dharashiv blocked the Dhule-Solapur highway near Yedshi carrying withered soybean and demanding a drought declaration. In Lohara, thousands marched with tractors and bullock carts seeking Rs 1 lakh per hectare aid, a cattle subsidy and loan waiver, and Washim and Beed saw rallies on 16 September.
alerts.impact: Rasta-roko is the stated tactic, so treat the Dhule-Solapur corridor near Yedshi as intermittently blockable with little notice. Keep a Solapur-Tuljapur-Latur alternate live and avoid single-route dependency for Dharashiv and Latur FM beats.

alerts.title: Monsoon retreating: withdrawal line at Jaisalmer-Nagaur-Sikar, Saurashtra-Kutch dry in three to four days
alerts.summary: The southwest monsoon withdrew from parts of West Rajasthan on 19 September, two days after the normal date. As of 22 September the withdrawal line runs through Jaisalmer, Nagaur, Sikar, Rohtak, Patiala and Gurdaspur, and IMD says conditions favour retreat from the rest of Rajasthan and parts of Saurashtra and Kutch over the next three to four days. IMD Ahmedabad's 22 September forecast gives dry weather across all Saurashtra-Kutch districts with only isolated light rain in Surendranagar, Jamnagar, Morbi, Dwarka and Kutch. The national cumulative rainfall deficit stood at 15%.
alerts.impact: Restore normal cut-offs and full FM pickup slots across Rajasthan and Saurashtra-Kutch - Jodhpur, Bikaner, Jaipur, Rajkot, Jamnagar and Bhuj pincodes can come off weather watch. This is the window to rebuild capacity ahead of the Navratri and Diwali peak.

alerts.title: East MP heavy rain from Sep 24: Chhatarpur, Panna, Satna, Shahdol, Mandla, Balaghat, Seoni, Chhindwara; peak Sep 25-26
alerts.summary: IMD forecasts heavy rain on 24 September in Chhatarpur, Panna, Satna, Umaria, Shahdol, Dindori, Mandla, Balaghat, Seoni and Chhindwara, while west Madhya Pradesh does not carry the same warning. The Bay of Bengal system's impact is expected to peak on 25-26 September with heavy to very heavy rain across most of eastern MP. The state has already received about 90% of its seasonal monsoon quota.
alerts.impact: Relax SLAs for eastern MP rural pincodes (Mandla, Dindori, Balaghat, Seoni, Shahdol) for 25-26 September and route Jabalpur-bound line-haul in daylight. West MP (Indore, Bhopal, Ujjain) should run near normal.

alerts.title: Deep depression crossed coast near Kalingapatnam (Srikakulam) overnight 23-24 Sep; weakening while moving NNW via south Odisha towards Chhattisgarh
alerts.summary: IMD said the deep depression crossed the north Andhra Pradesh–south Odisha coast close to southwest of Kalingapatnam in Srikakulam district between 11 pm on 23 Sep and 1 am on 24 Sep, with winds of 55-65 kmph gusting to 75 kmph. It entered Odisha via Rayagada and Koraput and is forecast to move north-northwest and weaken into a depression, passing Nabarangpur–Kalahandi–Balangir–Bargarh into Chhattisgarh. Odisha says 37 blocks, 160 GPs and 237 villages in six districts were affected and 8,082 people evacuated; Puri remains a 'red zone' with sea bathing banned for two days. Update (25 Sep afternoon): IMD confirmed the system has weakened further into a depression over south interior Odisha, with the rain belt continuing to track towards Kalahandi-Bargarh and Chhattisgarh; red-warning districts have narrowed to Nabarangpur, Kalahandi and Koraput.
alerts.impact: Landfall phase is over but the rain belt now shifts inland: keep SLA relaxation on south Odisha (Koraput, Rayagada, Malkangiri, Nabarangpur, Kalahandi) and north coastal AP (Srikakulam, Vizianagaram, Alluri) pincodes through 26 Sep, and pre-alert Chhattisgarh (Bastar division, Raipur-Durg belt) hubs for 25-26 Sep. Restart coastal FM pickups in Vizag/Srikakulam only after local route checks.

alerts.title: Red alert for Srikakulam, Vizianagaram and Parvathipuram Manyam; extremely heavy rain 23-24 September
alerts.summary: Srikakulam, Vizianagaram and Parvathipuram Manyam are under red alert for extremely heavy rain on 22-23 September, with the downpour peaking again on 23-24 September across those districts plus Alluri Sitharama Raju. District officials are on high alert and holidays have been declared. One death was reported: M. Hemantha Krishna of Vijayawada drowned in the overflowing Thotapalli canal at Seethanagaram mandal, Parvathipuram Manyam district. An orange alert for 24 September covers Kakinada, Konaseema, East and West Godavari and Eluru, with Visakhapatnam, Anakapalle, Krishna, Guntur, NTR and Bapatla on yellow. NDRF has five teams at Visakhapatnam, Srikakulam, Vizianagaram and Yanam.
alerts.impact: Flag Srikakulam, Vizianagaram, Parvathipuram Manyam and Alluri Sitharama Raju rural pincodes non-serviceable for 23-24 September and hold the Godavari delta - Kakinada, Konaseema, Eluru - on extended TAT for the 24th. Pause Vizag hub outbound overnight and restart only after the system clears inland.

alerts.title: South Chhattisgarh braces for extremely heavy rain on 24 September; Bastar, Bijapur, Sukma flagged
alerts.summary: With the weakening deep depression tracking from south Odisha into Chhattisgarh, the state is under an extremely-heavy-rain warning for 24 Sep and very-heavy-rain warnings for 25 and 26 Sep, with thundersqualls of 50-60 kmph gusting to 70 kmph. South Chhattisgarh — Bastar, Dantewada, Sukma and Bijapur — is expected to see heavy to very heavy rain at some places; residents of low-lying areas have been told to watch for rising streams and waterlogging.
alerts.impact: Treat Bastar-division pincodes (Jagdalpur, Dantewada, Sukma, Bijapur, Narayanpur) as high-risk for LM on 25-26 Sep — interior nala crossings go under quickly; keep COD/RTO buffers and inform carriers of possible NH-30/NH-63 slowdowns. Raipur–Durg–Bilaspur FM hubs may see thunderstorm-related delays.

alerts.title: Bihar: orange alert in 19 districts, yellow in 19 more as depression remnant brings rain Sep 24-26
alerts.summary: The Meteorological Centre, Patna has put all Bihar districts on alert for 24 September - 19 under orange and 19 under yellow - with heavy rain at isolated places, lightning and 40-50 kmph gusts. Weather is forecast to stay poor from 24 to 26 September as the Bay of Bengal deep depression moves inland. The state is already carrying a severe flood season, with the Ganga, Kosi and Gandak above danger marks at several gauges earlier this month.
alerts.impact: Expect FM pickup slippage and LM attempt failures across Bihar on 24-26 September, worst in already-flooded riverine blocks of Bhagalpur, Khagaria, Katihar and Saran. Keep extended TAT on Kosi-Gandak belt pincodes and run Patna hub outbound in morning windows before afternoon thunderstorms.

alerts.title: Cloudburst-type downpours hit Poonjar, Erattupetta, Vagamon and Vattavada; 10 dead, high ranges cut
alerts.summary: Extremely intense localised convective downpours - described as cloudburst-like rather than monsoon-trough driven - battered Poonjar, Erattupetta, Vagamon, Kuttikkanam and Vattavada near Munnar on 22 September, triggering widespread landslides. Regina Johnny and her son Josephine Johnny died when their house at Poonjar Payyanithottam collapsed, and soil and gravel blocked the Poonjar-Adivaram road at Peringulam. Total deaths across Malappuram, Kottayam and Idukki reached 10. Idukki's minister-in-charge Anoop Jacob asked travellers to postpone all non-essential travel to the high ranges, with relief camps opened at Pazhampillichal Government LP School and the LP School at Palisakkallu.
alerts.impact: Treat Idukki and eastern Kottayam high-range pincodes - Poonjar, Erattupetta, Vagamon, Kuttikkanam, Munnar and Vattavada - as non-serviceable or extended-TAT until roads are confirmed clear. Because the pattern is cloudburst-driven, forecast alerts will not reliably precede the blockage, so hold buffer stock at Kottayam and Thodupuzha rather than pushing daily into the hills.

alerts.title: Bengaluru IT corridor waterlogged at Marathahalli, KR Puram and Kadubeesanahalli after a second day of rain
alerts.summary: A second consecutive day of heavy showers on 22 September caused severe traffic, waterlogging and tree falls across Bengaluru. Water accumulated at Thubarahalli, Varthur Kodi, the BGS Flyover, Marathahalli, Kadubeesanahalli and KR Puram, all on the eastern IT corridor. The city observatory logged 15.9 mm in the 24 hours to 8:30 am and traffic police advised alternative routes.
alerts.impact: Bengaluru east LM - Whitefield, Marathahalli, Bellandur, KR Puram and Varthur pincodes - will run 60 to 90 minutes behind on rain evenings, so shift those beats earlier and re-sequence around Varthur Kodi and the BGS flyover. Move FM pickups from Whitefield seller clusters into morning slots.

alerts.title: Dikchu-Mangan road cut at Zin Khola and 5th Mile; even transhipment is not possible
alerts.summary: Major landslides at Zin Khola and 5th Mile have completely halted travel between Dikchu and Mangan in North Sikkim, and transhipment - walking goods across the slide to a waiting vehicle - is not possible at Zin Khola. Clearance crews were waiting for rain to abate before deploying heavy machinery. This is a second North Sikkim connectivity failure alongside the NH-10 Bardang restriction.
alerts.impact: Mangan and North Sikkim pincodes should be flagged non-serviceable rather than extended-TAT, because no transhipment workaround exists at Zin Khola. Stop accepting new North Sikkim orders until a reopening is confirmed.

alerts.title: NH-29 Kohima-Dimapur degraded: one side blocked at Sechu Zubza, seven points fully blocked
alerts.summary: Nagaland Post reports one side of NH-29 blocked by a landslide at Sechu Zubza, with roughly seven strategic points where one carriageway is completely blocked and at least 15 more partially blocked, alongside drainage failure and extensive potholes. Nagaland Police have issued diversions: Kohima to Dimapur via Jotsoma-Khonoma-Mezoma-Sechuma-Sechu Zubza or Dzudza Bridge-Mezo Basa-Sechuma-Sechu Zubza, and Dimapur to Kohima via Peducha Bridge-Tsiesema on the 10 Mile Road.
alerts.impact: Dimapur-Kohima is Nagaland's main freight artery and is now single-carriageway at multiple points - add two to three hours per run and route per the police diversions. This also degrades Dimapur as a staging option for Manipur-bound volume held back by the UNC blockade.

alerts.title: UFBU 3-day nationwide bank strike Sep 28-30; branches effectively shut for five days from Sep 26
alerts.summary: The United Forum of Bank Unions, which claims to represent 90% of the banking workforce, has confirmed it will go ahead with a three-day nationwide strike from 28 to 30 September after conciliation before the Deputy Chief Labour Commissioner remained inconclusive. The core demand is a five-day banking week. Because the strike follows the fourth Saturday and Sunday, branches may be unavailable for normal customer-facing work for five consecutive days from 26 to 30 September. SBI has advised customers to complete important transactions in advance and to use ATMs, Customer Service Points, internet banking, YONO, mobile banking and UPI. SBI has issued a customer advisory for the 28-30 September strike, and the unions have warned of an indefinite nationwide strike from October 26 if the dispute is not resolved.
alerts.impact: COD remittance, cash deposit and branch-dependent settlement cycles for Delhivery, Shadowfax and Xpressbees delivery partners will stall from 26 to 30 Sep - pre-fund partner float and move DP payouts to digital rails before 25 Sep. Expect cash-handling friction at rural CSP-dependent LM hubs; the window also overlaps month-end, so clear vendor payments and FM pickup-agent settlements ahead of it.

sources.name: NewsX - Bank Strike 2026, 3-day nationwide strike from Sept 28 (ground report, TV)

alerts.title: Alluri Sitharama Raju agency: night heavy-vehicle ban on ghat roads; KK-line express trains halted Sep 23-24
alerts.summary: Police have restricted night movement of heavy vehicles on ghat roads in the agency areas of Alluri Sitharama Raju district because of landslide risk from the deep depression's rainfall. East Coast Railway has suspended several express services on the Visakhapatnam-Kottavalasa-Kirandul (KK) line on 23 and 24 September. Vizianagaram district has declared a school holiday for 23 September on the collector's orders. Red alerts are in force for Srikakulam, Parvathipuram Manyam and Vizianagaram, orange for Visakhapatnam, Anakapalli and Alluri Sitharama Raju, and yellow for Kakinada, Eluru, the combined Godavari districts and Krishna. Officials have warned that road transport and even helicopter services may have to be curtailed.
alerts.impact: Do not schedule overnight line-haul on the Araku, Chintapalli, Paderu or Rampachodavaram ghat sections until 25 Sep. Rail-fed FM/LM legs in Vizianagaram, Parvathipuram Manyam and Alluri districts lose the KK-line feed for two days - shift to road only where the ghat ban allows, and pre-flag Araku and Paderu tribal-belt pincodes as extended-SLA or temporarily non-serviceable.

alerts.title: Odisha: vehicle curbs on Kalinga Ghat (Ganjam-Kandhamal); red warning for Rayagada, Koraput, Gajapati, Ganjam
alerts.summary: IMD has issued a red warning for Rayagada, Koraput, Gajapati and Ganjam for 23 and 24 September, with very heavy to extremely heavy rain across south Odisha and an extremely-heavy-rainfall alert running until 25 September. The state government has restricted vehicular movement on certain roads including Kalinga Ghat, which connects Ganjam and Kandhamal. Rescue teams are deployed in Ganjam, Gajapati, Koraput, Malkangiri, Rayagada, Kalahandi and Bolangir, and educational institutions are shut until 24 September in Nabarangpur, Malkangiri, Puri, Jagatsinghpur, Ganjam, Gajapati, Koraput and Khurda. Fishermen are barred from the sea until 24 September.
alerts.impact: The Kalinga Ghat curb severs the shortest Berhampur-Phulbani link - route Kandhamal-bound freight via Bhanjanagar or Boudh instead. Treat Rayagada, Koraput, Gajapati, Ganjam and Malkangiri pincodes as non-serviceable for 23-24 Sep, hold Berhampur and Jeypore LM attempts, and keep Bhubaneswar as the staging hub rather than pushing stock into south Odisha branches.

alerts.title: Assam: Brahmaputra swallows much of Roumari Pathar village in Barpeta; Barkhetri residents on night watch
alerts.summary: Severe erosion has continued for nearly a month at Roumari Pathar in Barpeta district, where the Brahmaputra has reportedly swallowed a major portion of the village along with public institutions, farmland and the homesteads of hundreds of families. Riverbank erosion along the Brahmaputra is also keeping residents of Barkhetri awake at night. Statewide, erosion by the Brahmaputra and its tributaries has wiped out close to 330 villages over a decade and affected 23,369 families between 2016 and 2026, with Dhubri worst hit at 5,241 families and the river widening there by 4.64 km; Morigaon, South Salmara-Mankachar and Barpeta are the other hardest-hit districts.
alerts.impact: Retire address masters for eroded habitations in Roumari Pathar and the Barkhetri belt rather than carrying them as repeat failed-attempt pincodes - this is a structural serviceability loss, not a weather event. Rebase Barpeta, Dhubri, Morigaon and South Salmara LM beat plans on surviving villages, and avoid siting new 3P last-mile touchpoints inside the active erosion corridor.

alerts.title: Himachal: fresh slide halts Chailchowk-Tattapani road in Mandi; Chandigarh-Manali highway back to one-way
alerts.summary: A fresh landslide stopped traffic for three hours on the Chailchowk-Tattapani road in Mandi district. Officials counted 60 blocked roads statewide that day, with Mandi worst hit at 33, followed by Kangra at 10 and Kullu at nine. Feeder stretches toward Kullu have seen episodic slides through the month, adding unpredictability to transit times. A separate 24-hour landslide block on the Chandigarh-Manali highway has since been cleared to one-way traffic. The weather office expects light rain with isolated showers in the middle hills.
alerts.impact: Build a 12-24 hour buffer into Mandi and Kullu LM promise dates - the Chailchowk, Karsog and Tattapani belt pincodes are the most exposed. Send Manali-bound line-haul only in daylight while the Chandigarh-Manali highway runs one-way, and hold off on new 3P LM expansion in interior Mandi until the monsoon fully withdraws.

alerts.title: Gajapati keeps 140 identified landslide-prone spots under watch; 6 cyclone and 264 temporary shelters readied
